title: Appointment reminder worker with draining shutdown
name: Appointment reminder worker

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this worker finishes its in-progress reminders when it receives SIGTERM? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: track awaits loadAppointment before adding the job's promise to inFlight. A job that has been claimed but is still loading its appointment is invisible to shutdown: the loop exits, inFlight looks empty (or smaller than reality), drain resolves, and pool.end() runs while that query or the subsequent send/complete is still pending. That job then fails mid-way (possibly after the SMS was sent but before complete), so the patient may get a duplicate reminder when the lease expires. The promise should be registered in inFlight immediately when the job is claimed, covering the load too.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Two worker processes call claimNext at the same moment while a single job is due. What happens?
choices: One claims it; the other's subquery skips the locked row and returns null
Both claim it and both send the reminder
Both block until the first transaction commits, then the second claims it too
The second gets a serialization error and crashes
choiceQuestions.explanation: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED makes the second query skip the row the first has locked, so it returns no job. There is no double claim, no blocking wait (that's what SKIP LOCKED avoids), and no serialization error at the default isolation.

choiceQuestions.prompt: With concurrency = 4 and four reminders already running, what does the polling loop do?
choices: Claims a fifth job and queues it in memory
Waits until any running reminder finishes, then rechecks
choiceQuestions.explanation: When inFlight.size >= concurrency it awaits Promise.race(this.inFlight), which resolves once any one finishes, then continues. It doesn't claim more, the idle sleep is only for empty queues, and the loop only exits on stopping.

choiceQuestions.prompt: notifier.send throws for a job. What eventually happens to that job?
choices: It is retried by this worker immediately
It stays pending and becomes claimable again once its 2-minute lease expires
choiceQuestions.explanation: The catch only logs; status stays 'pending' with locked_until set. claimNext picks rows whose locked_until < now(), so after the lease lapses any worker can retry it. Nothing marks it skipped, retries immediately, or deletes it.
